senses.def: a narrow beam of light, heat, or other energy
examples: The first rays of sunlight came through the curtains.
UV rays can damage your skin even on cloudy days.

senses.def: a small amount of something good, such as hope
examples: The new drug offers a ray of hope to patients with the disease.

note: "Catch some rays" (informal) = sunbathe. A ray is also a flat sea fish (vatoz).

senses.def: to arrive at a place, or to get to a particular level or point
examples: We reached the hotel just after midnight.
Temperatures could reach 100 degrees this weekend.

senses.def: to succeed in making a decision or agreement after discussion
examples: The jury reached a verdict after two days.

senses.def: to stretch out your arm to touch or get something, or to contact someone
examples: I can't reach the top shelf without a ladder.
You can reach me on my cell phone after six.

senses.def: the distance you can stretch your arm, or how far something's influence goes
examples: Keep all medicines out of the reach of children.

note: No preposition after the verb: "reach the city", not "reach to the city". "Reach out" = make contact to offer or ask for help.

senses.def: to behave or change in a particular way because of something that happens
examples: How did your parents react when you told them the news?
Markets reacted badly to the announcement.

senses.def: to change chemically when mixed with another substance, or to become ill from a food or drug
examples: Iron reacts with water and oxygen to form rust.
Some patients react badly to the medication.

note: Use "react to" something. "React against" means to rebel against something.

senses.def: what you do, say, or feel because of something that has happened
examples: Her first reaction was to laugh.
The new policy got a mixed reaction from teachers.

senses.def: an illness or bad effect caused by a food or drug
examples: He had a severe allergic reaction to peanuts.

senses.def: a chemical change produced when substances are mixed
examples: The experiment shows a chemical reaction between vinegar and baking soda.

senses.def: to look at written words and understand them, or to say them aloud
examples: I read about the earthquake in the newspaper.
She reads her kids a story every night.

senses.def: to have particular words written on it, or to show a measurement
examples: The sign read "No parking after 6 p.m."
The thermometer read minus ten.

senses.def: to understand or interpret something in a particular way
examples: She's very good at reading people's emotions.

note: Irregular: read /riːd/ – read /red/ – read /red/. Same spelling, different pronunciation.

senses.def: a person who reads, especially one who reads a lot or reads a particular publication
examples: She's a big reader and finishes a novel every week.
The magazine has over a million readers.

senses.def: a device that reads data, such as cards or electronic books
examples: Swipe your card through the reader to pay.

senses.def: easily and quickly, without difficulty
examples: Fresh vegetables are readily available at the local market.
The information is readily accessible online.

senses.def: willingly and without hesitating
examples: He readily admitted that he had made a mistake.

note: Pronounced /ˈredɪli/, like "ready", not like "read" /riːd/.

senses.def: the activity of reading, or the skill of reading
examples: Reading is my favorite way to relax.
The program helps children improve their reading.

senses.def: a text you are asked to read, or an event where someone reads aloud to an audience
examples: The professor gave us forty pages of reading for Monday.
The author is giving a reading at the bookstore tonight.

senses.def: a number shown by a measuring device, or a way of understanding something
examples: The nurse took a blood pressure reading.

senses.def: fully prepared to do something, or finished and available to use
examples: Are you ready to go? The taxi's outside.
Dinner will be ready in ten minutes.

senses.def: willing to do something
examples: She's always ready to help her neighbors.
I'm not ready to give up yet.

senses.def: actually existing or happening, not imagined
examples: The movie is based on a real story.
Climate change is a real threat to coastal cities.

senses.def: not artificial or fake, or the true one rather than what is claimed
examples: Is that ring made of real gold?
The real reason he quit was the long commute.

senses.def: (informal, American) very
examples: That was real nice of you to drive me home.

note: "For real?" (informal) = really? "Real estate" = property such as houses and land (emlak).

senses.def: sensible and accepting what is actually possible
examples: Let's be realistic; we can't finish the project in a week.
Set realistic goals so you don't get discouraged.

senses.def: showing things as they are in real life
examples: The video game has incredibly realistic graphics.

senses.def: the true situation as it actually is, not as you would like it to be
examples: In reality, most startups fail within five years.
The dream of owning a house is far from reality for many young people.

note: "Reality TV" = shows about real people. "A reality check" = a reminder of how things really are.

senses.def: the moment or process of understanding something you did not know before
examples: There's a growing realization that the plan won't work.
The realization that she had left her passport at home hit her at the airport.

senses.def: the act of achieving a hope or plan
examples: Opening the restaurant was the realization of a lifelong dream.

senses.def: to understand or become aware of a fact or situation
examples: I didn't realize you were coming today.
She suddenly realized she had left the oven on.

senses.def: to achieve something you hoped or planned for
examples: He finally realized his dream of becoming a pilot.

note: Trap: "realize" means "fark etmek", not "gerçekleştirmek" in most contexts. British spelling: realise.

senses.def: used to make an adjective, adverb, or verb stronger
examples: The concert was really good.
I really need a vacation.

senses.def: used to say what is actually true
examples: What really happened that night?
Nobody really knows why the dinosaurs died out so quickly.

senses.def: used to show surprise or interest
examples: "I'm moving to Japan." "Really? When?"

note: "Not really" is a soft way to say no: "Do you like it?" "Not really."

senses.def: an area of activity, interest, or knowledge
examples: The idea belongs in the realm of science fiction.
She has made important contributions in the realm of public health.

senses.def: (formal or literary) a country ruled by a king or queen
examples: The king traveled to every corner of his realm.

note: "Within the realm of possibility" = possible. The "a" is silent: /relm/.

senses.def: the back part of something
examples: The kitchen is at the rear of the house.
Please exit through the rear of the bus.

senses.def: at or near the back of something
examples: The car's rear window was smashed.
Kids should always ride in the rear seat.

senses.def: to care for young children or animals until they are grown
examples: The farm rears sheep and cattle for meat.

note: "Bring up the rear" = be at the back of a group. "Rear-end" (verb) = crash into the back of a car.

senses.def: a cause or explanation for something that happens or that someone does
examples: What was the reason for the delay?
There's no reason to panic.

senses.def: the ability to think clearly and make sensible judgments
examples: He wouldn't listen to reason and drove home anyway.
Science is based on reason and evidence.

senses.def: to form a judgment by thinking logically
examples: She reasoned that the store would be less crowded in the morning.

note: Say "the reason for" or "the reason why/that", not "the reason of".

senses.def: fair, practical, and sensible
examples: It's a reasonable request; let's give them the extra day.
Any reasonable person would have called the police.

senses.def: not too expensive
examples: The hotel was clean and the prices were very reasonable.

senses.def: fairly good, but not very good
examples: There's a reasonable chance we'll finish on time.

note: "Beyond a reasonable doubt" is the standard of proof in US criminal trials.

senses.def: fairly or to a degree that is acceptable but not very high
examples: The test was reasonably easy.
I'm reasonably sure that the store closes at nine.

senses.def: in a fair and sensible way
examples: Try to discuss the problem calmly and reasonably.
The apartments are reasonably priced for the area.

senses.def: the process of thinking logically, or the reasons and arguments behind an opinion
examples: I don't follow your reasoning; why would sales go up in winter?
The test measures logical reasoning and problem-solving skills.

senses.def: to make someone feel less worried or afraid
examples: The doctor reassured her that the surgery was routine.
Officials tried to reassure the public that the water was safe.

senses.def: a person who fights against the government of their country
examples: Rebels seized control of the northern city.
Government troops clashed with rebel forces near the border.

senses.def: a person who refuses to follow normal rules or behave as expected
examples: She was a bit of a rebel in high school.

senses.def: to fight against authority or refuse to obey rules
examples: Teenagers often rebel against their parents' rules.

note: Stress: noun REB-el /ˈrebl/, verb re-BEL /rɪˈbel/.

senses.def: an attempt by a group of people to change their government using violence
examples: The army crushed the rebellion within weeks.
The rebellion began when soldiers refused to fire on protesters.

senses.def: opposition to authority or to accepted ways of behaving
examples: Dyeing his hair green was a small act of teenage rebellion.

senses.def: to build something again after it has been damaged or destroyed
examples: It took the town ten years to rebuild after the hurricane.
The church was rebuilt using the original stones.

senses.def: to make something strong or successful again
examples: After the scandal, the company worked hard to rebuild trust with customers.

note: Irregular: rebuild – rebuilt – rebuilt.

senses.def: to remember something, especially in order to tell others about it
examples: I don't recall meeting him before.
She recalled how her father used to take her fishing.

senses.def: to ask people to return a faulty product, or to order someone to come back
examples: The company recalled 50,000 cars because of faulty brakes.

senses.def: an official request to return a product, or the ability to remember
examples: The recall affects all models made before 2023.
He has total recall of every game he's ever played.

collocations: as far as I can recall
note: More formal than "remember". Followed by -ing: "I recall seeing her".

senses.def: a piece of paper or email that shows you have paid for something
examples: Keep the receipt in case you need to return the shoes.
Can I get a receipt, please?

senses.def: (formal) the act of receiving something
examples: Please confirm receipt of this letter.
Payment is due within 30 days of receipt of the invoice.

note: The "p" is silent: /rɪˈsiːt/.

senses.def: to get something that someone gives or sends you
examples: Did you receive my email yesterday?
She received an award for her work with refugees.

senses.def: to react to something in a particular way, or to experience a type of treatment
examples: The new album was well received by critics.
Three people received treatment for minor injuries.

note: Spelling: "i before e except after c": receive, not recieve.

senses.def: the part of a phone that you hold to your ear and mouth
examples: She picked up the receiver and dialed the number.
He slammed the receiver down in anger.

senses.def: a piece of equipment that receives radio or TV signals
examples: We bought a new receiver for the home theater system.

senses.tr: alan kişi, alıcı; (Amerikan futbolu) pas alan oyuncu
senses.def: a person who receives something, or a football player who catches passes
examples: The wide receiver caught the ball in the end zone.

senses.def: happening or starting a short time ago
examples: Prices have gone up a lot in recent years.
In a recent interview, the director talked about her next film.

senses.def: not long ago
examples: I recently moved to Seattle for a new job.
Until recently, few people had heard of the app.

note: Often used with the present perfect: "I have recently started...", but past simple is also common in American English.

senses.def: the area near the entrance of a hotel or office where visitors go first
examples: Please leave your key at reception when you check out.
Ask at reception for a visitor's pass.

senses.def: a formal party to welcome someone or celebrate something, such as a wedding
examples: The wedding reception was held in a garden by the lake.

senses.def: the way people react to something, or the quality of radio or phone signals
examples: The proposal got a cool reception from investors.
There's no cell phone reception in the mountains.

note: In American hotels, reception is usually called the "front desk".

senses.def: a period when a country's economy is weak, with less trade and more unemployment
examples: Many small businesses closed during the recession.
Economists warn that the country could slip into recession next year.

note: A "depression" is a longer and more severe recession.

senses.def: a set of instructions for cooking a dish, with a list of ingredients
examples: This is my grandmother's recipe for apple pie.
I found a great recipe for vegetarian chili online.

senses.def: a way of doing something that is likely to lead to a particular result
examples: Spending more than you earn is a recipe for disaster.

note: Pronounced in three syllables: /ˈresəpi/. Trap: a doctor's prescription is NOT a recipe (reçete = prescription).

senses.def: a person who receives something
examples: She was the youngest recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize.
Check the recipient's address before you send the email.

note: Formal. Opposite: donor (in medicine) or sender (for mail).

senses.def: (informal) to think or believe something
examples: I reckon it's going to rain later.
How much do you reckon the repairs will cost?

senses.def: to calculate something approximately, or to consider someone or something to be something
examples: The painting is reckoned to be worth over a million dollars.

collocations: a force to be reckoned with
note: "I reckon" is informal and sounds British or rural/Southern American. "A force to be reckoned with" = a powerful competitor.

senses.def: the act of knowing who someone is or what something is when you see or hear it
examples: He looked at me without any sign of recognition.
The phone uses facial recognition to unlock.

senses.def: public praise for someone's work, or official acceptance that something is true or legal
examples: She received recognition for her years of volunteer work.
There is growing recognition that mental health matters at work.

note: "Changed beyond recognition" = changed so much it cannot be recognized.

senses.def: to know who someone is or what something is because you have seen or heard it before
examples: I didn't recognize you with short hair!
She recognized the song from the first few notes.

senses.def: to accept that something is true, or to officially accept something as legal or valid
examples: The government recognized that mistakes had been made.
Many countries refuse to recognize the new regime.

senses.def: to show official appreciation for someone's work or achievements
examples: The award recognizes outstanding teachers in the state.

note: British spelling: recognise.

senses.def: to say that someone or something is good or suitable
examples: Can you recommend a good dentist near here?
I highly recommend the fish tacos.

senses.def: to advise someone to do something
examples: Doctors recommend that adults get at least seven hours of sleep.
We recommend booking early in the summer.

note: Spelling: one c, double m. Pattern: "recommend doing" or "recommend that someone do", not "recommend someone to do" (less common).

senses.def: an official suggestion about the best thing to do
examples: The committee made several recommendations to improve safety.
We chose the hotel on a friend's recommendation.

senses.def: a statement that someone is suitable for a job or course
examples: Her professor wrote her a strong letter of recommendation.

senses.def: the process of building or putting something back into its former state
examples: The reconstruction of the bridge will take two years.
Billions of dollars are needed for postwar reconstruction.

senses.def: an attempt to show how a past event happened using the available evidence
examples: Police staged a reconstruction of the crime to help witnesses remember.

note: "Reconstruction" (capital R) refers to the period after the US Civil War (1865–1877).

senses.def: written or stored information about something, kept for the future
examples: The hospital keeps medical records for every patient.
There is no record of the payment in our system.

senses.def: the best result ever achieved, or the known facts about someone's past
examples: She broke the world record in the 200 meters.
The company has an excellent safety record.

senses.def: to write down or store information, or to save sound or pictures
examples: The band recorded their first album in a garage.
The meeting was recorded so absent staff could watch it later.

note: Stress: noun REC-ord /ˈrekərd/, verb re-CORD /rɪˈkɔːrd/. "Off the record" = not for publication.

senses.def: sound or pictures that have been recorded
examples: Police released a recording of the emergency call.
This is the best recording of the symphony I've heard.

senses.def: the process of recording music or other sounds
examples: The recording of the album took six months.

senses.def: (formal) to tell someone about something that happened, especially your own experience
examples: In her memoir, she recounts her childhood on a farm in Iowa.
He recounted the events of that night to the police.

senses.def: to count something again, especially votes
examples: The votes were recounted after the result was challenged.

senses.def: a second count of votes in an election
examples: The losing candidate demanded a recount.

note: "Count again" meaning is pronounced /ˌriːˈkaʊnt/; the noun is /ˈriːkaʊnt/.

senses.def: to get well again after an illness, injury, or shock
examples: It took her months to recover from the accident.
He's still recovering from the flu.

senses.def: to return to a normal or stronger state after a difficult period
examples: The economy is slowly recovering after the crisis.

senses.def: to get back something that was lost or stolen
examples: Police recovered the stolen paintings in a warehouse.
I managed to recover the deleted files.

senses.def: the process of becoming healthy again after an illness or injury
examples: The surgeon expects him to make a full recovery.
Recovery from knee surgery can take several months.

senses.def: the process of returning to a normal or better state
examples: The country's economic recovery has been slower than expected.

senses.def: the act of getting back something that was lost or stolen
examples: The reward led to the recovery of the stolen jewels.

note: "In recovery" often means getting treatment for addiction.

senses.def: to find new people to join a company, organization, or the armed forces
examples: The company plans to recruit 200 new engineers this year.
Terrorist groups use social media to recruit young people.

senses.tr: acemi asker, yeni eleman, yeni üye
senses.def: a person who has recently joined the army, police, or an organization
examples: New recruits spend ten weeks in basic training.
The team's latest recruit scored on his debut.

senses.tr: işe alım, personel alımı, askere alma
senses.def: the process of finding new people to join a company, organization, or the armed forces
examples: The hospital is struggling with the recruitment of nurses.
The army launched a new recruitment campaign aimed at college graduates.

note: Americans often say "hiring" in everyday business contexts.

senses.def: to process used materials so they can be used again
examples: We recycle all our bottles, cans, and newspapers.
Only a small percentage of plastic is actually recycled.

senses.def: to use an idea, method, or thing again, often in a new way
examples: The movie just recycles old jokes from the first film.

senses.def: having the color of blood or fire; also used for a face that is flushed or for orange-brown hair
examples: She was wearing a bright red coat.
His face went red with embarrassment.

senses.def: the color of blood or fire, or red wine
examples: The walls were painted a deep red.
Would you like red or white with dinner?

note: "In the red" = owing money. "Red tape" = bureaucracy (bürokrasi). "See red" = become very angry. In US politics, red = Republican.
